items.author: BIJU MATHEW
items.description: Walking in major Indian cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, and Bengaluru presents numerous challenges for pedestrians. Effective solutions involve creating uninterrupted footpaths and prioritizing pedestrian needs during urban planning.

items.title: Minnesota court reverses reopening of 300-acre farm estate over 1989 will
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: In a significant Minnesota inheritance case, the state Court of Appeals has reinstated a 2017 ruling concerning the estate of farmer Clarence Vatthauer. Disputes arose from conflicting wills dated 1982 and 1989, leading to a previous court's decision being vacated. The appeals court's ruling underscored the necessity of procedural compliance and the need for finality in estate administration, reshaping the understanding of inheritance law.

items.title: Beyoncé's childhood Houston home sold in May 2026 after $1.275m listing
items.author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
items.description: Beyonce's childhood home in Houston, Texas, found a buyer after being listed for $1.275 million in April 2026. Her family purchased the 1935 property in 1987 and lived there until 1994. The 4,010-square-foot house has undergone extensive renovations, including upgrades to its kitchen, bedrooms and outdoor spaces. Its connection to the singer attracted multiple offers and interest from fans across the United States.

items.title: Giacometti chandelier bought for £250 later sold for £2.922m in 2023
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: A chandelier created by Alberto Giacometti sold for £2.922 million at a Christie's auction in February 2023. Originally purchased for £250 by British artist John Craxton in the 1960s, it remained in his family until his death. The chandelier was commissioned by art patron Peter Watson for the literary magazine Horizon, which published many famous authors. It underwent extensive authentication process before its auction, confirming its historical significance.

items.title: Double-digit growth seen on corporate scoreboard in Q2, but bank, IT, pharma lag
items.description: September quarter earnings exhibited significant revenue and profit growth for various companies in key sectors. Revenue rose by 22.1% with net profit increasing by 27.5%, surpassing the previous quarter. However, banking, IT, and pharmaceuticals sectors experienced a slow down in growth rates. Excluding lending, operating margins improved, indicating stronger performance in non-banking sectors. Analysts expect 13 out of 18 sectors to deliver double-digit sales growth in the coming quarters.

items.title: India valuations hit 6-year low, but stocks still expensive than EM peers
items.description: India's equity valuations have reached their lowest levels in six years after a recent market decline. Factors contributing to this decline include foreign selling, a weaker rupee, and rising crude prices. Despite lower valuations, overseas investors remain hesitant to invest in Indian equities due to comparative valuations. The MSCI India Index trades at a premium compared to other emerging markets, influencing foreign investor sentiment.

items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: A 5,610-acre section of Hendrie Ranch will remain undeveloped due to a $12.9 million conservation easement. It is part of Florida's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program to safeguard agricultural properties.

items.title: Banks pass on rate hikes, but go slow when rates fall; RBI study finds
items.author: TNN
items.description: A recent study by the RBI indicates that banks are more responsive to interest rate hikes than to cuts. Specifically, banks relayed 76.4% of repo rate increases, while only 64% of reductions were passed on. Amid periods of tightening, lending rates surged significantly, in contrast to the minimal decreases observed during easing. This research highlights the intricate dynamics of interest rate adjustments, particularly affecting sectors like MSMEs.

items.title: Joan Eardley painting resurfaces at charity shop, later sells for £29,500
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: In an unexpected twist, a stunning landscape painting by Scottish talent Joan Eardley was discovered in an English charity shop. Named Summer Fields, the artwork fetched an impressive £29,500, with proceeds dedicated to funding medical research. After a paper label revealed its authenticity, the piece was returned to Scotland for further evaluation. This sale highlights the increasing appreciation for Eardley’s influence on mid-20th century art, celebrated in various exhibitions.

items.description: પૂર્વ સુપ્રીમ કોર્ટના ન્યાયાધીશ સંજય કિશન કૌલે પૂર્વ CJI ડી.વાય. ચંદ્રચૂડના વલણની ટીકા કરી છે. તેમણે કહ્યું કે ચંદ્રચૂડ ન્યાયાધીશોની નિમણૂકના મામલે સરકાર તરફ જરૂર કરતાં વધુ ઝૂકેલા હતા. જસ્ટિસ કૌલે પોતાની આવનારી પુસ્તક ‘વિથાઉટ ફિયર ઑર ફેવર’માં સુપ્રીમ કોર્ટની છ ખાલી જગ્યાઓ ભરવા માટે યોજાયેલી કોલેજિયમ બેઠકનો ઉલ્લેખ કર્યો છે. જસ્ટિસ કૌલે કહ્યું કે કોલેજિયમે સરકારના દબાણનો વિરોધ કરવો જોઈએ. આજે નિમણૂકો પહેલાં સરકાર સાથે નામો અંગે ચર્ચા કરવાની પરંપરા બની ગઈ છે. જસ્ટિસ કૌલે પોતાના પુસ્તકમાં લખ્યું છે…
